title: Geometric Imbalance in Semi-Supervised Node Classification

strengths: The paper addresses a practically important problem. Retrieving existing unlabeled nodes avoids synthesizing node features and graph topology, and remains applicable when a minority class has only one labeled example.

The reported evaluation is broad: five datasets, three GNN architectures, several imbalance ratios, and naturally imbalanced settings. Some improvements are substantial; Table 1 reports CiteSeer-GCN F1 of 64.94 versus 56.32 for the strongest listed baseline.

The pseudo-label accuracy diagnostics, component ablations, and sensitivity analyses provide useful evidence beyond aggregate classification scores. The observation that embedding geometry can complement biased classifier confidence is valuable.

The appendix supplies dataset distributions, pseudocode, training settings, and hyperparameter search ranges. No material ethical concern is apparent from the described use of established benchmark datasets.
weaknesses: Experimental reporting contains substantive inconsistencies. In Table 8, GCN at imbalance ratio 5 has 11,593.60 aligned and 2,308.40 discarded nodes, totaling 13,902 despite only 13,632 unlabeled nodes. Table 9 reports 94.20 ± 8.04 accuracy for SAGE at ratio 50 as a standard error over five repetitions; bounded accuracies with that mean cannot have a standard error exceeding 5.80. Corrected tables and per-run results are needed to establish confidence in these diagnostics.

Originality is insufficiently distinguished from prior self-training methods. The paper itself describes M3S as filtering pseudo-labels through agreement with clustering assignments, closely resembling DPAM, but provides no explicit controlled comparison. The DPAM-plus-confidence ablation is a useful partial comparison; stronger comparisons with M3S and simple fixed-weight rank fusion are still needed to establish the contribution of the proposed machinery. Baseline coverage also stops at 2022, weakening the state-of-the-art claim for NeurIPS 2025.

The geometric filtering definition is inconsistent. Equation 5 measures distance to the assigned class center, while Section 4.3 assumes this is the node's nearest class center. Assigning an entire cluster by its centroid does not guarantee that property for individual nodes. Equation 7 also needs precise per-node rank semantics and justification for its confidence weight, which decreases as RBO increases beyond 0.5 despite the stated motivation.

Important reproduction and computational details remain unresolved. Algorithm 1 does not explicitly enforce the per-class addition cap or update the remaining unlabeled pool, and retraining initialization is unspecified. No code link or selected configurations are supplied. With 40–100 rounds, up to 2,000 epochs per subsequent round, and repeated clustering, runtime and measured memory comparisons are necessary to substantiate the computational advantages.

The conclusions overstate the consistency of the evidence. UNREAL loses both metrics for GraphSAGE on Computers-Random and balanced accuracy for GAT on Flickr. Table 11 shows mixed component benefits, including degradation from DGIN and negligible gains over geometric ranking in some settings. Additionally, changing training splits and majority-label counts at higher imbalance ratios prevents attributing cross-ratio trends solely to imbalance. These limitations, together with the reporting and comparison gaps, outweigh the promising performance gains.

strengths: The paper addresses an important problem: node classification with extremely scarce minority-class labels. Retrieving existing unlabeled nodes avoids synthesizing node features and edges and provides a practical alternative to graph oversampling.

The evaluation spans five datasets, three GNN architectures, multiple imbalance ratios, and naturally imbalanced settings, with five repetitions and reported standard errors. Several gains are substantial: on CiteSeer with GCN at imbalance ratio 10, F1 improves from the best baseline's 56.32 to 64.94.

The pseudo-label diagnostics provide useful evidence about minority-class error amplification and the potential value of combining classifier predictions with embedding geometry. The appendix includes component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and substantial training and dataset details.
weaknesses: The contribution is insufficiently distinguished from its closest predecessor. Section 6 explicitly describes M3S as filtering pseudo-labels through agreement with clustering assignments, closely matching DPAM, but provides no experimental comparison. Comparisons with M3S and equally tuned class-balanced self-training are essential to establish the additional contribution.

The mathematical specification contains a consequential inconsistency. Equation 5 measures distance to the assigned class center, whereas Section 4.3 assumes this is necessarily the nearest class center. Assignment through a cluster center in Equation 4 does not guarantee that property for individual nodes. Equation 7 also needs an explicit definition of how ordered node lists become aligned numerical ranks before combination.

Evidence for the additional ranking and filtering mechanisms is mixed. In Table 11, the full method improves over geometric ranking alone by only 0.59 F1 on Cora and 0.06 on PubMed; removing DGIN improves CiteSeer F1 from 57.51 to 58.71. These results do not support uniformly beneficial components. A fixed-weight ranking combination would also help establish whether RBO-based weighting is necessary.

Reporting inconsistencies undermine confidence in the supporting experiments. In Table 8, GCN at imbalance ratio 5 reports 11,593.6 aligned and 2,308.4 discarded nodes, totaling 13,902 despite only 13,632 unlabeled nodes. Claims of consistent superiority also contradict Tables 2 and 6: UNREAL loses on Computers-Random with GraphSAGE and on Flickr balanced accuracy with GAT. These discrepancies require correction and verification.

The imbalance-trend experiments change more than imbalance alone. Ratios 20, 50, and 100 retain one minority label per class while increasing majority labels, and the citation datasets switch training-split construction at the larger ratios. This supports comparisons within each setting but weakens causal claims about degradation as imbalance increases.

Computational and reproduction details remain incomplete. Appendix D permits 40–100 training rounds with up to 2,000 epochs per later round, but provides no end-to-end runtime or measured memory comparison. Selected configurations, precise class-selection rules, and executable code are not supplied. Together with the missing closest-method comparison and unresolved reporting errors, these gaps outweigh the promising reported gains.
